source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The ESP32 operates at up to 160MHz, reduces to 80MHz while idle using automatic light sleep, and only goes into deep sleep (~10µA) when the battery is critical or after a false wake. Its wake sources are a timer (5min) and the touch button (GPIO 26 ext0). However, in the final version I will definitelly keep it in deep sleep most of the time and wake it only for updates.
Does that mean we need to relocate some PINs? Maybe AXP IRQ?

value_updates.final_deep_sleep_policy: remain in deep sleep most of the time and wake only for updates

routing_warnings.description: The question about relocating pins and AXP IRQ concerns GPIO allocation rather than the sleep-policy values established by the same message.
The boost EN question concerns control of the switched 5V rail rather than ESP32 sleep and wake behavior.
The proposed pull-down on the boost converter EN pin concerns the switched 5V rail's default-off behavior.
